SRC-351:R001.text: A foreign protocol command is refused with a typed FOREIGN_PROTOCOL_COMMAND that names the protocol owner, the full invocation and the route to run instead, and is never refused as a bare unknown command.

SRC-351:R002.text: The refusal names the owning protocol, the exact requested command, and carries next_action guidance, so the caller cannot read it as a typo.

SRC-351:R003.text: SAIPEN verbs and shortcuts (cc, continue, next, status) remain SAIPEN-owned and unaffected by foreign-protocol routing.

SRC-351:R004.text: A malformed or absent exact_namespace block degrades to the old refusal without inventing an owner.

SRC-351:R005.text: The router and registry suites are unaffected by the exact-namespace declaration.

SRC-351:R006.text: Never present a foreign protocol as a candidate for an explicit SAIPEN command; an explicit /saipen <cmd> must never be dispatched to a skill whose name merely resembles it, and exact namespace ownership is decided before semantic skill matching.

SRC-351:R007.text: A NO_HOME or similar refusal from a foreign protocol must not trigger a working-directory change into another protocol repository, a sibling-repo search, or the creation of that protocol home.

SRC-351:R008.text: Re-read the installed skills directory on session start so a stale inventory cannot map a namespace to the wrong owner.

SRC-351:R009.text: The FreeBuff host stops offering a substitute protocol for an explicit SAIPEN command.

SRC-351:R010.text: A live /saipen continue in _BZ_REA on FreeBuff executes the SAIPEN route end to end.
